$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of RFC 9162. Source .cache/rfc-9162.txt (RFC 9162, Certificate Transparency Version 2.0, sha256 a0e432ce7580c99fcc8faf0cf3f6191f9ce6b4864f949158e020d4ecb295081f). RFC 9162 Section 5 gives these messages in prose and ships no JSON Schema. INSTANCE: the 2xx JSON response of get-entries (Section 5.6). The entries array may be empty (Section 5.6: because of skew the log MUST return an empty entries array). SOURCE AMBIGUITY: the Outputs list in Section 5.6 indents sth under entries, so as printed each entry object has an sth member, but the text also says in any case the log server MUST return the latest STH it knows about, which cannot sit inside an empty entries array. This schema therefore requires a top-level sth (inferred) and permits, without requiring, an sth inside each entry as printed. submitted_entry is 'JSON object equivalent to inputs that were submitted to submit-entry': submission, type, chain, with the trust anchor added to chain if not submitted. Instances are JSON values as received; binary fields stay base64 text and are not decoded (RFC 4648 Section 4, per Section 5). A pattern ^AQ[...] on a TransItem field binds the first two decoded octets, the VersionedTransType code of Section 4.5, because base64 of 0x01 0x0T begins AQ (every code here has 0 in its high nibble) and the low nibble T confines the third character to a block of four, its other two bits coming from the next octet; hence four characters per code in each pattern. The pattern states what a v2 log emits; it is not a client acceptance test, since a v2 client MUST NOT construe a non-v2 SCT (rfc-9162#R-0069) or an unrecognized TransItem type (rfc-9162#R-0079) as an error. Fields the RFC does not define are allowed (Section 5: any fields not understood SHOULD be ignored). A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. This schema cannot check the TransItem body, signatures, or any cross-field relation: those are in ../messages.yaml (constrained_by and notes per field).
title: get-entries response body (GET <Base URL>/ct/v2/get-entries) (DERIVED)

base64.$comment: RFC 4648 Section 4 alphabet with padding; at least one octet (Section 5: binary data is base64 encoded according to Section 4 of RFC 4648).

transItem_entry.$comment: base64 of a TransItem of type x509_entry_v2 (0x0100) or precert_entry_v2 (0x0101), Section 4.5 / 4.3

transItem_sct.$comment: base64 of a TransItem of type x509_sct_v2 (0x0102) or precert_sct_v2 (0x0103), Section 4.8

transItem_sth.$comment: base64 of a TransItem of type signed_tree_head_v2 (0x0104), Section 4.10
